title: shode-house scope manifest (Milestone E -- ROADMAP-runtime-10.md SS7.1-7.3, bd: shode-roadmap/C-E1)
description: Per-bd concurrency scope lock. `agents[].owns` = SS7.1 scope manifest. `shared_files` = SS7.2 shared-file strategy (exclusive/append-only/merge-owner/generated -- data-driven, no filename is hardcoded in scripts/scope-check.sh). `base_sha` = SS7.3 optimistic-conflict snapshot store, written only by `scope-check.sh ... --snapshot`, never hand-edited. This file is a REFERENCE (schema + example) only -- the live manifest that scripts/scope-check.sh actually reads lives at .shode-house/scope/<bd-id with / -> -->.json inside a project that opted into shode-house (same convention as .shode-house/state/*.json for scripts/workflow-state.sh). Read by script/CI only -- never preloaded into an agent context.

schema_version.description: bump when the shape below changes; scripts/scope-check.sh may refuse to read an unknown version rather than guess (NO MAGIC).

bd_id.description: matches the bd-id passed as scope-check.sh's first argument. Slashes are encoded as '--' in the manifest FILENAME only (not in this field).

agents.description: SS7.1 scope manifest -- one entry per concurrently-active agent instance for this bd (e.g. 'Dave#1', 'Dave#2', 'Chris'). First matching owns[] pattern wins; two entries should never own an overlapping path -- that is an authoring error scope-check.sh cannot resolve for you (fix the manifest, not the script).

agent.description: free-form agent identity string, matched byte-for-byte against scope-check.sh's <agent> argument -- same identity the Scope Contract (references/scope-lock.md) was posted under.

owns.description: shell case-pattern strings (same glob dialect as the Scope Contract's 'Files:' field, e.g. 'src/orders/**'). `*` already matches across '/' in this dialect -- there is no filesystem-globstar distinction to configure.

shared_files.description: SS7.2 shared-file strategy. Keyed by a case-pattern path (same dialect as owns[]). Checked BEFORE agents[].owns[] -- an explicit shared-file strategy always wins over an implicit ownership glob.

mode.description: exclusive: only `owner` may write, denies everyone else, same as merge-owner's access rule but intended for files nobody should ever co-edit (e.g. a single generated-but-checked-in fixture). merge-owner: only `owner` writes directly; other agents must route their change through the owner instead of writing the path themselves. append-only: any agent registered in this bd's agents[] may write (concurrent appends to a journal-like file do not need a single owner). generated: nobody hand-writes this at all -- always denied, message points at `regenerate_via`.

owner.description: required when mode is exclusive or merge-owner; must equal one of agents[].agent for the DENY message to name someone real.

regenerate_via.description: required when mode is generated -- the command that actually produces this file, so a DENY message is actionable instead of a dead end.

coupled_with.description: optional -- other paths whose content this file's correctness silently depends on. --snapshot / --verify also snapshot/check these paths together with the primary one. This is the direct fix for the ac632a3 incident (see example.manifest.json): a CI step in the plugin repository's ci.yml assumed its golden.json scenario file's old schema while a different, correctly scope-locked agent changed golden.json under its own Files -- neither agent's Scope Contract overlapped, so nothing in SS7.1 alone would have caught it. Declaring the coupling here means a --verify on ci.yml also reports CONFLICT if golden.json drifted, even though the writer only touched ci.yml.

note.description: free-text rationale, shown nowhere by the script -- documentation for humans reading the manifest.

base_sha.description: SS7.3 optimistic-conflict snapshot store. Written only by `scope-check.sh <bd-id> <agent> <path> --snapshot`; read only by `--verify`. Keyed by agent, then by path, to a sha256 hex digest (or the literal string ABSENT if the file did not exist at snapshot time). Not part of what a human author fills in when creating a manifest.
